title: Genetic studies with a uracil DNA glycosylase biosensor support a role for mitochondrial UNG1 in nuclear uracil repair.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplementary package (2.34 MB). It contains exactly one PDF (gkag852_supplemental_file.pdf, 9 pages, text extracted with pypdf) plus 10 figure images (.gif/.webp). The PDF holds Supplementary Table S1 (a list of PCR/cloning oligonucleotide sequences), Supplementary Table S2 (UNG genotypes of ~8 CRISPR knockout clones), and Supplementary Figures S1-S6 (flow cytometry plots, fluorescence microscopy panels, immunoblots). There is no CSV, TSV, XLSX, FCS or any other machine-readable data file anywhere in the package. Searched the full text (52 kB) for 'GEO', 'SRA', 'deposit', 'github', 'Zenodo', 'figshare': zero hits. The Europe PMC accession scan and the Zenodo/Dryad DOI search returned nothing except one RefSeq transcript ID (NM_080911.3, the human UNG2 messenger RNA used for cloning).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Experimental details taken from the methods text only: three technical replicate wells per condition (n = 3, mean +/- standard error), two cell backgrounds (293T and U2OS), and knockout clones for UNG1, UNG2 and UNG1/2. The underlying per-cell flow cytometry events and per-image intensity values are described but were never deposited, so I could not count them.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified by opening the files. The data availability statement says only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material'. The entire supplement is one 9-page PDF of figures plus two small text tables, and figure images. No numeric data file exists to download; the measurements live only inside plot images.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no table with a measured outcome column anywhere. The quantity of interest (ratio of green fluorescent protein to mCherry red fluorescent protein median intensity) appears only as bar heights in figure panels and would have to be reconstructed by digitising plots.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL. The only sequences present are ~15 cloning primers (Table S1) and short knockout allele descriptions in Human Genome Variation Society notation (Table S2). No per-example feature table of any kind.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated clearly in the figure legends (median fluorescence intensity ratio, normalised integrated intensity, fold change, hours post-transfection) - but they describe plotted figures, not a data file.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL by a wide margin. Counting generously from the figure legends, the whole paper reports on the order of 50-100 condition-by-replicate measurements (about 8 knockout clones x 2 cell lines x plus/minus uracil glycosylase inhibitor x 3 technical replicates). The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small - but small because there is essentially no data, which is the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No discrepancy found: the supplement contains exactly the tables and figures the text cites (S1-S2, S1-S6). Nothing is missing relative to what the paper promises; the paper simply never promises a dataset.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label provenance is clean in principle - fluorescence read on an Incucyte SX5 live-cell imager and a flow cytometer, a genuine physical measurement, not another model's output. It is just never released in numeric form.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be trained from this paper: the only quantitative outputs are bar charts in a PDF, so any claim would rest on digitised pixels from roughly 50 measurements.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use cell genotype and treatment to predict how much uracil a cell removes from its chromosomal DNA.
plain_idea.train_on: What the model would see per example: which uracil-DNA glycosylase isoform is knocked out (UNG1, the mitochondrial form; UNG2, the nuclear form; or both), the cell background (293T or U2OS), and whether the uracil glycosylase inhibitor protein Ugi is present. Verified count of such examples: roughly 50-100, read off figure legends, with no numeric file.
plain_idea.predict: The biosensor readout - the ratio of green fluorescent protein to mCherry red fluorescent protein median intensity, measured by flow cytometry and live-cell imaging 48 hours after transfection, which rises when uracil excision is blocked.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Drug-discovery groups targeting UNG for cancer therapy would want to know which isoform to inhibit; but with ~50 measurements and three input variables, a lookup table answers this better than any model, so there is no project here.

ml_idea: None viable. The only machine-learning-shaped idea the paper suggests - predicting uracil excision activity from genotype and inhibitor state - has three categorical inputs and about 50 plotted measurements, which is a two-row summary table, not a model. A separate, better-resourced idea (predicting cytosine base editor editing efficiency from target sequence) is already covered by DeepBE, BE-DICT and DeepABE/DeepCBE and uses none of this paper's data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated beyond the supplement size, because no feature/label table can be built: the measurements exist only as plotted bars in a PDF.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the Europe PMC supplementary package and list the file types. It took two minutes and killed the candidate: one PDF, ten images, zero tabular files.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A killers A1, A2, A3 and A5, all verified by opening the files. The entire 'data' is a 9-page supplementary PDF holding a primer list, a knockout-genotype table, and flow cytometry/microscopy figures; there is no numeric data file, no outcome column, and on the order of 50-100 measurements in total. Nothing was deposited in any repository. This is a well-executed wet-lab biosensor paper whose output is a method and a biological conclusion, not a dataset.
